recentEvents.title: At least 64 children killed and 64 injured in Yemen as intensified hostilities approach three-month mark
recentEvents.ai_summary: The update reports a significant escalation in hostilities in Yemen since early September, resulting in at least 64 children killed and 64 injured, with fighting intensifying around densely populated areas such as Taiz and Lahj. This sustained violence and rising civilian casualties underscore a deteriorating security environment, justifying continued or heightened pre-evacuation measures and increased humanitarian concern.
recentEvents.diff_before: <div class="tag country">Countries: Yemen, Djibouti</div> <div class="tag source">Source: European Commission's Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations</div> <p><img src="https://reliefweb.int/sites/default/files/styles/thumbnail/public/previews/f5/46/f546bddf-44d2-5e49-b5d4-5adec59795a6.png" alt></p> <p>Please refer to the attached Map.</p>
recentEvents.diff_after: <div class="tag country">Country: Yemen</div> <div class="tag source">Source: UN Children's Fund</div> <p><strong>NEW YORK, 18 November 2026 –</strong> At least 64 children have been killed and 64 injured in Yemen since hostilities escalated on 3 September. The number of casualties is likely to increase as renewed fighting continues around densely populated areas, particularly in Taiz and Lahj.</p> <p>“The rising number of children killed and injured in Yemen is devastating. It must stop,” said UNICEF Executive Director, Catherine Russell.

recentEvents.title: DR Congo: Compte rendu de la réunion mensuelle du mois d'octobre 2026
recentEvents.ai_summary: The update highlights ongoing nutritional challenges in DR Congo, including low reporting levels and unmet nutritional needs amid the Ebola response. While this signals humanitarian stress, there is no indication of escalating conflict or security threats requiring heightened travel or evacuation measures.
recentEvents.diff_before: <div class="tag source">Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees</div> <p><img src="https://reliefweb.int/sites/default/files/styles/thumbnail/public/previews/51/61/5161ef01-c67c-54e1-a5e7-1337706dd120.png" alt></p> <p>Please refer to the attached Infographic.</p>

Les échanges ont porté sur la méthodologie de calcul des personnes dans le besoin pour le HNRP 2027, la préparation de la revue annuelle 2026 du PRONANUT, la réponse nutritionnelle à Ebola dans les CTE/CT et les interventions des partenaires.</p> <p>Les discussions ont mis en évidence un faible niveau de rapportage et des besoins nutritionnels encore non couverts.

recentEvents.title: Afghanistan: Humanitarian Update, October 2026
recentEvents.ai_summary: The humanitarian situation in Afghanistan is deteriorating due to widespread displacement impacting children’s food security and health, compounded by significant funding shortfalls threatening winter aid delivery. While no direct conflict escalation is reported, the increased vulnerability and logistical challenges elevate the risk environment, warranting reconsideration of travel and operational plans.
recentEvents.diff_before: <div class="tag source">Source: Save the Children</div> <p><strong>KABUL, 18 November 2026</strong> <em>–</em> More than half of children displaced in Afghanistan said they have less food to eat since leaving their homes, while two in five reported worsening health, according to a new Save the Children report that reveals the severe toll displacement is taking on children across the country.</p> <p>The “Children on the Move” report, based on interviews with more than 800 children and caregivers in seven provinces in Afghanistan, found that displacement over the past three years has deepened hunger, disrupted education and exposed children to heightened protection risks. More than nine in 10 children surveyed had experienced displacement or migration.</p>
recentEvents.diff_after: <div class="tag source">Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs</div> <p><img src="https://reliefweb.int/sites/default/files/styles/thumbnail/public/previews/ed/cb/edcbaa74-4196-486d-9476-6da74de9cf7e.png" alt></p> <p>Please refer to the attached file.</p> <p><strong>Funding shortfalls threaten winter response in Afghanistan</strong></p> <p>As temperatures begin to fall across Afghanistan, humanitarian partners are ramping up winter preparedness amid significant funding constraints. Aid organizations are pre-positioning supplies to enable them to deliver assistance before access to remote communities becomes more challenging.
